units.title: Unit 1: Personal Profiles, Upbringing & Life History

lessons.title: Past Simple vs Past Continuous
grammar: Past Simple for completed past actions and main storyline events
Past Continuous for background actions in progress (was/were + -ing)
Interrupted actions using when and while
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-001"
pronunciation: [{"point":"Past simple -ed endings","explain":"Distinguish between /t/, /d/, and /ɪd/ endings for regular past tense verbs.","examples":[{"pattern":"worked / played / started","ipa":"/wɜːkt/ / /pleɪd/ / /ˈstɑː.tɪd/","word":"started"}],"visual":"🗣️"}]
cando: "Can narrate a simple past event and describe background actions using when and while"
lessons.recycled: Foundational communication & basic level vocabulary

lessons.title: Past Habits & Life Experiences (Used to & Present Perfect)
grammar: Used to + infinitive for past habits and states no longer true
Present Perfect with ever and never for life experiences
Contrast between Past Simple (finished time) and Present Perfect (unfinished time)
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-002"
pronunciation: [{"point":"The used to liaison","explain":"The final d in used and initial t in to blend into a single /tuː/ sound.","examples":[{"pattern":"used to","ipa":"/ˈjuːs.tə/","word":"used to"}],"visual":"🔗"}]
cando: "Can describe past habits and talk about general life experiences"
lessons.recycled: Past Continuous for background actions in progress (was/were + -ing), Interrupted actions using when and while, Milestone

lessons.title: Obligation & Rules in Housing (Have to / Must / Mustn't)
grammar: Have to / don't have to for external obligation and lack of obligation
Must for strong personal obligation; Mustn't for prohibition
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-003"
pronunciation: [{"point":"Silent t in mustn't","explain":"Practice saying mustn't cleanly without pronouncing the middle t.","examples":[{"pattern":"mustn't","ipa":"/ˈmʌs.ənt/","word":"mustn't"}],"visual":"🏠"}]
cando: "Can discuss housing rules, lease conditions, and tenant obligations"
lessons.recycled: Present Perfect with ever and never for life experiences, Contrast between Past Simple (finished time) and Present Perfect (unfinished time), Graduate

lessons.title: Describing Homes & Prepositions of Place
grammar: Prepositions of place and location (opposite, next to, between, across from)
There is / There are with quantifiers (some, any, several)
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-004"
cando: "Can describe property layouts, room features, and neighbourhood locations"
lessons.recycled: Have to / don't have to for external obligation and lack of obligation, Must for strong personal obligation; Mustn't for prohibition, Heating

lessons.title: Workplace Tasks & Verb Collocations (Do vs Make)
grammar: Workplace verb collocations: do business/research vs make a decision/effort
Present Simple vs Present Continuous for current projects vs regular job duties
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-005"
pronunciation: [{"point":"Office vocabulary stress","explain":"Primary stress placement in workplace terms (dePARTment, PROductive, EFFICient).","examples":[{"pattern":"department","ipa":"/dɪˈpɑːt.mənt/","word":"department"}],"visual":"💼"}]
cando: "Can talk about job duties, office projects, and everyday work responsibilities"
lessons.recycled: Prepositions of place and location (opposite, next to, between, across from), There is / There are with quantifiers (some, any, several), Downtown

lessons.title: Present & Past Passive in Workplace Processes
grammar: Present Simple Passive (is/are + past participle) for workflow routines
Past Simple Passive (was/were + past participle) for completed reports and tasks
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-006"
cando: "Can describe office procedures and task status using simple passive forms"
lessons.recycled: Workplace verb collocations: do business/research vs make a decision/effort, Present Simple vs Present Continuous for current projects vs regular job duties, Responsible

lessons.title: Describing Health Symptoms & Giving Advice (Should / Shouldn't)
grammar: Should / shouldn't for health recommendations
Expressing physical symptoms (have got a headache, feel dizzy, hurt)
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-007"
pronunciation: [{"point":"Silent l in should","explain":"The letter l in should and shouldn't is silent (/ʃʊd/, /ˈʃʊd.ənt/).","examples":[{"pattern":"should","ipa":"/ʃʊd/","word":"should"}],"visual":"🏥"}]
cando: "Can explain illness symptoms and give appropriate health advice using should"
lessons.recycled: Present Simple Passive (is/are + past participle) for workflow routines, Past Simple Passive (was/were + past participle) for completed reports and tasks, Client

lessons.title: Healthy Lifestyle & Physical Wellbeing
grammar: Adverbs of degree and frequency (extremely, fairly, regularly, rarely)
Imperatives for fitness and wellbeing instructions
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-008"
cando: "Can discuss dietary habits, exercise routines, and personal wellbeing goals"
lessons.recycled: Should / shouldn't for health recommendations, Expressing physical symptoms (have got a headache, feel dizzy, hurt), Treatment

lessons.title: Booking Travel & Asking for Information (Indirect Questions)
grammar: Indirect questions for polite enquiry (Could you tell me where... / Do you know if...)
Modals for polite requests (Could I, Would you mind)
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-009"
pronunciation: [{"point":"Polite intonation in indirect questions","explain":"Using gentle rising-falling pitch contours when asking polite service questions.","examples":[{"pattern":"Could you tell me...?","ipa":"/kʊd juː tel miː/","word":"Could"}],"visual":"✈️"}]
cando: "Can book travel arrangements, ask polite questions, and handle hotel check-in"
lessons.recycled: Adverbs of degree and frequency (extremely, fairly, regularly, rarely), Imperatives for fitness and wellbeing instructions, Habit

lessons.title: Sightseeing & Prepositions of Movement
grammar: Prepositions of movement (along, across, through, past, towards)
Imperatives and directional phrases for giving directions
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-010"
cando: "Can ask for and give directions to urban landmarks and describe sightseeing tours"
lessons.recycled: Indirect questions for polite enquiry (Could you tell me where... / Do you know if...), Modals for polite requests (Could I, Would you mind), Luggage

lessons.title: Comparing Options (Comparatives & Superlatives)
grammar: Comparative and superlative adjectives (cheaper, more expensive, the best, as...as)
Modifying comparatives (a bit cheaper, much better)
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-011"
cando: "Can compare products, evaluate prices, and make smart purchasing decisions"
lessons.recycled: Prepositions of movement (along, across, through, past, towards), Imperatives and directional phrases for giving directions, Historic

lessons.title: Too & Enough / Indefinite Pronouns
grammar: Too + adjective / Adjective + enough for suitability
Indefinite pronouns (someone, anything, nowhere, everybody)
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-012"
cando: "Can express customer preferences, report defective items, and ask for refunds"
lessons.recycled: Comparative and superlative adjectives (cheaper, more expensive, the best, as...as), Modifying comparatives (a bit cheaper, much better), Afford

lessons.title: Future Plans & Intentions (Will vs Be Going To)
grammar: Be going to for intentions and planned tech upgrades
Will for spontaneous decisions, predictions, and tech promises
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-013"
pronunciation: [{"point":"Weak form of going to","explain":"In casual conversation, going to frequently reduces to gonna /ˈɡən.ə/.","examples":[{"pattern":"going to","ipa":"/ˈɡən.ə/","word":"gonna"}],"visual":"📱"}]
cando: "Can discuss technology habits, device preferences, and planned digital updates"
lessons.recycled: Too + adjective / Adjective + enough for suitability, Indefinite pronouns (someone, anything, nowhere, everybody), Replace

lessons.title: First Conditional in Tech & Daily Life
grammar: First conditional: If + Present Simple, Will + infinitive
Time clauses with when and as soon as
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-014"
cando: "Can explain cause-and-effect conditions and basic cybersecurity rules"
lessons.recycled: Be going to for intentions and planned tech upgrades, Will for spontaneous decisions, predictions, and tech promises, Connection

lessons.title: Gerunds vs Infinitives in Learning Goals
grammar: Verbs followed by gerund (-ing): enjoy, practice, mind, consider
Verbs followed by infinitive (to + verb): decide, hope, plan, want, agree
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-015"
cando: "Can express educational goals, learning strategies, and personal ambitions"
lessons.recycled: First conditional: If + Present Simple, Will + infinitive, Time clauses with when and as soon as, Option

lessons.title: Second Conditional Intro (Hypothetical Dreams)
grammar: Second conditional intro: If + Past Simple, Would + infinitive for imaginary situations
If I were you, I would...
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-016"
cando: "Can talk about hypothetical future situations and offer personal advice using second conditional"
lessons.recycled: Verbs followed by gerund (-ing): enjoy, practice, mind, consider, Verbs followed by infinitive (to + verb): decide, hope, plan, want, agree, Achieve

lessons.title: Defining Relative Clauses (Who, Which, That, Where)
grammar: Defining relative clauses: who for people, which/that for things, where for places
Omitting relative pronouns when they are object of the clause
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-017"
cando: "Can describe movies, books, venues, and cultural events using relative clauses"
lessons.recycled: Second conditional intro: If + Past Simple, Would + infinitive for imaginary situations, If I were you, I would..., Advice

lessons.title: Question Tags & Social Agreement
grammar: Question tags for checking information and seeking agreement (is it?, don't you?)
So / Neither for expressing agreement (So do I / Neither am I)
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-018"
pronunciation: [{"point":"Intonation on question tags","explain":"Falling intonation expects agreement; rising intonation asks a real question.","examples":[{"pattern":"Great concert, wasn't it?","ipa":"/wɒz.ənt ɪt/","word":"wasn't it"}],"visual":"🎭"}]
cando: "Can maintain social conversation, express agreement, and use natural question tags"
lessons.recycled: Defining relative clauses: who for people, which/that for things, where for places, Omitting relative pronouns when they are object of the clause, Review

lessons.title: Reported Speech Statements & Backshift
grammar: Reported speech for statements (He said that..., She told me that...)
Tense backshift rules (Present Simple -> Past Simple)
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-019"
cando: "Can report news, opinions, and environmental statements using reported speech"
lessons.recycled: Question tags for checking information and seeking agreement (is it?, don't you?), So / Neither for expressing agreement (So do I / Neither am I), Opinion

lessons.title: A2 General Course Master Review & Consolidation
grammar: Comprehensive review of all A2 grammar: past simple/continuous, present perfect, future forms, modals, conditionals, and passive voice
lessons.teacher_notes:
code: "EN-A2-020"
cando: "Can demonstrate full A2 language competency across conversational, professional, and practical everyday scenarios"
lessons.recycled: Reported speech for statements (He said that..., She told me that...), Tense backshift rules (Present Simple -> Past Simple), Protect
